R0139.title: Friendly Fraud / Chargeback Fraud
R0139.definition: A consumer maliciously initiates a chargeback with their bank or payment institution after legitimately receiving goods or services, falsely claiming non-receipt or unauthorized transaction, to obtain a refund while retaining the goods.
R0139.description:
Friendly fraud, also called chargeback fraud, is consumer-initiated payment dispute abuse. The consumer bypasses the merchant's normal after-sales approval and asks an issuer, acquirer, or payment platform to reverse the funds. Common patterns include falsely claiming non-delivery after receiving goods, denying a transaction completed by the cardholder or a family member, disputing a service without first contacting the merchant, and organized actors spreading repeated disputes across linked accounts, devices, and cards.

It differs from R0235 refund abuse: R0235 exploits merchant- or platform-controlled return, refund-without-return, and compensation processes, while friendly fraud exploits bank and payment-network dispute rules. Attackers may exploit difficult delivery proof for digital goods, confusing merchant descriptors, delayed cross-border tracking, or short response windows to increase dispute success. Controls require payment-authentication, device, login, delivery, service-fulfillment, and support evidence, followed by representment within card-network deadlines.
R0139.influence: Merchants may lose both goods and payment while paying dispute fees and card-network penalties; persistently high chargeback ratios can worsen acquiring terms or terminate payment access.

observables: A consumer initiates a chargeback with the bank after signing for the goods, claiming non-receipt or unauthorized transaction despite conclusive delivery signature records
The same cardholder or device repeatedly initiates chargebacks across multiple merchants, with a chargeback rate significantly higher than normal users
Chargebacks are initiated without any prior communication or return request to the merchant, going directly to the bank dispute process
After family member consumption, the cardholder concentrates chargebacks on similar small-value transactions citing unauthorized activity
